newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PLDT sets staff cut, rate restructuring.
newsitem.headline: PLDT sets staff cut, rate restructuring.

text.p: Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co (PLDT) hopes to overcome stiff competition and the effects of an impending cut in U.S. telephone rates by reducing staff and restructuring local and overseas call tariffs, officials said.

"We have to do all this to maintain our market strength. We have to change our (rate structure) because we are vulnerable to long distance calls," executive vice president Edgardo del Fonso told reporters after an analysts briefing on Monday.
PLDT is reducing its staff by 1,800 people to 16,473 by the end of this month. "We made a budget of 865 million pesos ($32.9 million) for this," del Fonso said.
The country's largest telephone network has trimmed its workforce by more than 1,000 since it started an employee reduction programme two years ago.
It plans to cut staff to 15,000 by the year 2000, said senior vice president Antonio Samson.
Del Fonso said net savings from the employee reduction programme were expected to hit 661 million pesos this year.
PLDT has also sought approval from the Philippine National Telecommunications Commission (NTC) to restructure its rates to meet competition with new carriers.

In its petition, PLDT proposed cutting its international toll rates to the United States to 121.50 pesos from the present 152.55 pesos for the first three minutes. It also sought to lower call rates to other countries such as Hong Kong, Japan and Saudi Arabia, where many Filipinos work.

U.S. telephone companies have been pressing for a steep cut in international tariffs in a bid to generate more calls. At present, the rate between the United States and the Philippines is $1 per minute and U.S. firms have sought to cut it to 38 cents per minute.
But PLDT has also sought rate increases for its basic local phone charges and plans to implement call metering to compensate for the international call reduction.
"We are proposing an increase in (local phone) rates to make our local service viable," said PLDT marketing manager Manny Lim.
PLDT subsidises domestic calls from revenues derived from international calls.
Del Fonso said the expected drop by 15 to 20 percent in U.S. call rates would result in an eight to 10 percent cut in PLDT's revenues this year.
PLDT posted a net income of 6.44 billion pesos last year from 5.751 billion in 1995 while its revenues increased to 28.616 billion pesos from 25.252 billion.
It has not made any official forecast for 1997's results.
International long distance calls accounted for 55 percent of PLDT's revenues last year, while 16 percent came from local long distance calls and 28 percent from its local calls.
PLDT says revenues derived from U.S. long distance calls dropped to 12 percent of total revenues last year from 24 percent in 1990.
The firm expects revenues from domestic calls to increase by seven to eight percent due to line expansion and its proposed rate hike. ($1 = 26.3 pesos)
